newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - March 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - U.S. ambassador in Beijing says he hopes Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui will not transit United States en route to Panama meeting.
Six arrested for suspected role in cop killing.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - Finance ministry to propose cancelling tax exemption for military, education personnel by end-1997.
LIBERTY TIMES - Stock market sets seven-year high.
Girl rescued after being kidnapped, sexually abused for six years.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Cabinet orders government workers not to trade stocks during working hours.
Worldwide stock markets rise after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan issues remarks easing fears of imminent interest rate hike.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - Alan Greenspan says Wall Street "properly priced" if assumptions about corporate profit growth are correct.
Economics ministry says joining World Trade Organisation by July "difficult".
